gameStory.articleHeadline: Broncos beat the Seahawks 17-14 in OT on Ja'Quan McMillian's pick, Wil Lutz's 53-yarder
gameStory.articleDescription: — The Denver Broncos are atrocious on offense, depleted on defense and shaky on special teams. All they do is find ways to win.
gameStory.articleStory: DENVER -- — The Denver Broncos are atrocious on offense, depleted on defense and shaky on special teams. All they do is find ways to win. Ja’Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold’s pass in overtime Thursday night and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal that gave the Broncos a 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. The Broncos emerged from a tough six-week season-opening stretch with a 4-2 record despite an injury-riddled roster and a shaky quarterback, and the Seahawks (3-3) lost for the second time in five days. They also matched their loss total from last season, when they won their second Super Bowl title. The Broncos won despite Bo Nix throwing for just 107 yards, J.K. Dobbins leading the rushing attack with a mere 41 yards and managing a meager three first downs and 168 yards of total offense — less than half the 353 yards piled up by the Seahawks. “I don't know why we can't really push the ball vertically right now,” Nix said. “But defenses are just sitting back and hanging out. ... Hopefully we find a way to get more out of it.” Nix was as honest as he's been to date in his postgame comments about Denver's scuffling offense. “We’re definitely capable, we’ve shown it," he said. "And, you know I don’t know where the disconnect is right now, to be honest with you. ... I just think we’re really, for some reason, struggling to find those explosive plays, and that’s what makes an offense really spectacular: Is finding explosive plays. And right now, we don’t have those.”

whatToWatch.text: Bounce-back road test: Seattle's 3-2 and coming off a loss, and Vegas still likes them as 2.5-point favorites in Denver — a rare vote of confidence for a visiting team, and a chance to prove the last one was a blip.

Pass rush meets pass rush: Seattle's getting home 2.8 times a game, Denver 2.6 — two defenses that live in the backfield. With a 40.5 total, oddsmakers are expecting a grinder where every sack and every stalled drive swings it.

Depth gets called on: five Seahawks are out, including Jalen Milroe, Brandon Pili and Avery Smith, and Denver's down five of its own with Sam Ehlinger and Tyler Onyedim sidelined. Defenses holding at 21 (SEA) and 22.2 (DEN) points allowed means whoever's next man up executes cleanest takes it.

recap.text: Seattle outgained Denver by nearly 200 yards in Mile High and still walked off empty. After falling behind 14-3 on short touchdown runs by J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, the Seahawks clawed back in the fourth on George Holani's 1-yard plunge and a Sam Darnold two-point strike to Rashid Shaheed, then tied it on Jason Myers' 34-yarder. But three giveaways haunted Seattle, and the last one was fatal: Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Darnold in overtime to set up Wil Lutz's 53-yard winner. The Seahawks drop to 3-3 and lose for the second time in five days.

newsBlurb.text: Seattle heads to Denver on a short week for a Thursday nighter it's already calling critical, and the message out of the building is blunt: the Seahawks believe they can be great, but they've left too much on the field to prove it yet. Reinforcements arrive in the kicking game, where wideout Irv Charles comes off injured reserve and back onto the 53 after missing the season's opening stretch. Clean it up in the thin air, and the talk starts matching the tape.
